event: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, challenge: Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots

ai_tools.role: wrote the code, the analysis scripts, the data-table build scripts, and drafts of the text

ai_tools.name: OpenAI models, through the Codex command-line tool
ai_tools.role: independently recounted the main numbers and fact-checked the talk

ai_tools.role: found word times to cut the team's recorded voice for the talk (no audio is in this repository)

not_ai_generated: hand-drawn Moe, Vee and scientist characters
audio_video: No AI-generated audio or video is part of this project.
outside_review: No outside expert in satellite fire data has reviewed the work.

web/.holds: the web app (globe page, fuller page and story, connector page, seven-slide demo page), its engine, data tables, pictures and number checks
web/.ai_use: Code, data-table build scripts and number checks written by Claude through Claude Code; page text drafted with Claude and edited by the team. Pictures in img/fire_detectives/ and img/explainer/ are AI-generated (FLUX.2 klein 4B, an AI image model by Black Forest Labs, run in ComfyUI) and carry a visible mark; img/characters/ is hand-drawn by team members; img/ending/ and img/slides/ are screen captures of the project's pages; img/qr/ are QR codes.
tools: FLUX.2 klein 4B run in ComfyUI (lesson pictures only)
web/.directed_and_reviewed_by: Directed and reviewed by the team, Spark Squad. The idea and every decision were the team's.
web/.in_file_metadata: one-line header comment in every code file (.js, .cjs, .css, .py) saying it was written with AI coding assistants under the team's direction; <meta name="ai-assistance"> in every HTML page; data files (.json) carry no per-file note; they are covered by this file and AI_USE.md
